Marissa — draft answers below (short form) and an initial TAM schedule. Attaching a populated worksheet and a one-page TAM roles summary for review.

Key points (short):
- TAM coverage model: 10am–6pm customer timezone standard coverage (Mon–Fri) + 24/7 severity-driven on-call escalation. Standard offering includes a named TAM (primary) and a shared secondary for redundancy.
- On-call rotations: weekly primary/secondary rotation within dedicated TAM pool; emergency pager triggers escalations to incident manager.
- Incident ownership: Redwood owns model runtime and platform remediation up to rollback/traffic diversion; customer owns app-level fixes unless Redwood's product change required. For cross-boundary work, we run an incident playbook with joint action items and an agreed SLA for RCA delivery.
- Notification channels: email (immediate), PagerDuty (push), and a daily incident bridge (Zoom) for Sev1 until stabilized.
- Notification timings (proposal):
  * Sev1: initial ack within 15 minutes, continuous updates every 30 minutes until recovery; RCA draft within 72 hours; final RCA within 14 days.
  * Sev2: ack within 1 hour, updates every 4 hours; RCA within 7 business days.

TAM schedule (example for FinEx):
- Named TAM (primary): Karthik Iyer — primary weekday contact 10:00–18:00 ET (Mon–Fri)
- Secondary TAM: Sean Gallagher — covers weekends and will act as escalation for nights
- Incident Manager (escalation lead): Evelyn Hart — available on-call for Sev1 escalations (PagerDuty)

Attachments included: RFI-Support-Questionnaire.xlsx (completed draft), TAM-Roles-OnePager.docx (internal).

Please review — I'll polish language for procurement once you all sign off.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI: TAM coverage, incident communications & escalation flow

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Please find Redwood's responses attached and summarized below. We aimed to be concise so your ops and procurement teams can slot this into the RFI quickly.

Executive summary (for procurement/internal ops):
- Named TAM + redundancy: Redwood assigns a named TAM as primary during customer business hours and a secondary TAM for redundancy. For FinEx, proposed primary and secondary are listed below.
- On-call and escalation: Redwood provides 24/7 escalation for Sev1 events via PagerDuty and a designated incident manager for cross-team coordination.
- Communications: Sev1 is acknowledged within 15 minutes and updates provided every 30 minutes; Sev2 acknowledged within 1 hour with 4-hour update cadence.
- Ownership split: Redwood owns platform remediation actions; FinEx owns application-level fixes. When platform changes are necessary, Redwood provides a mitigation plan and coordinates any hotfix or rollback.

Proposed FinEx TAM assignments (subject to final contracting):
- Primary TAM (weekday business hours): Karthik Iyer — karthik_iyer@redwood.com — 10:00–18:00 ET Mon–Fri
- Secondary TAM / weekend coverage: Sean Gallagher — sean_gallagher@redwood.com — weekend on-call & escalation support
- Incident Manager / Sev1 escalation lead: Evelyn Hart — evelyn_hart@redwood.com — on PagerDuty for Sev1 escalation

Incident notification templates and timings (excerpt):
- Sev1 (platform outage affecting production): Initial ack 15m; bridge within 30m; updates every 30m; RCA draft 72h; final RCA 14 days.
- Sev2 (partial degradation): Initial ack 1h; updates every 4h; RCA 7 business days.

Attachments included: RFI-Support-Questionnaire.xlsx (finalized answers), SOC2-Summary.pdf (redacted summary), Incident-Comm-Templates.docx (message templates).

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bR Redwood-FinEx-RFI-2027 (detailed answers and runbook excerpts).

If this looks good, we can schedule a 30-minute vendor ops call next week to walk through the bridge process and verify PagerDuty integrations. Suggested windows: 4/29 or 5/3.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Dir, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
